Welcome to Pocket Allowance Ledger — PAL for short. This interactive user guide walks through every major parent and kid-web flow so you can run the app with confidence.
PAL is a parent-managed token economy for ages six and up — local to the phone, with a kid companion on home Wi-Fi. It is not kid banking.
This guide uses a sample household named Reyes so you can follow along without setup. Kids Maya, about eight, and Jacob, about six.
When iOS asks for Local Network access, tap Allow — kid web requires it. Keep PAL in the foreground while a kid browser is connected; the local server pauses if the app is backgrounded.
Open PAL. The sample Reyes household is already loaded — family name Reyes, two kids ready on Home.
Family password for kid web is reyes — lowercase. Kid PIN for both children is one-two-three-four. You can also find these in Settings under Reviewer guide.
Use the chapter pills to jump ahead, or play straight through with synced narration. Previous and Next re-listen a single step.
PAL stays on your device — no cloud sync required for the core token economy. PocketBudJet expense bridges are out of scope here.
Next we open Settings for a quick orientation, then walk Home, Balances, kid web, Approvals, Reports, and Contracts.
Open Settings from the gear icon or the Settings tab. Scroll to Reviewer guide for demo credentials and a short suggested path through the app.
Reviewer guide lists the sample household, suggested steps, design notes, and what PAL intentionally does not do.
Step one: Home — tap Done on a contract and confirm the coin lands in Balances.
Step two: Kid web — sign in with reyes, Maya, PIN one-two-three-four, then tap I did it on a job.
Step three: Approvals — confirm or decline the kid report. Optional: request a reward from kid web and approve here.
The parent app has five bottom tabs: Home, Balances, Reports, Contracts, and Settings. Each tab maps to a major part of the token economy.
Home is where you tap Done on today's contracts — the core evening flow. Balances shows in-hand versus banked tokens per child.
Reports holds charts, first-week versus now comparisons, and coaching nudges. Contracts lists behavioral contracts and thinning schedules.
Settings covers kid web, reviewer guide, kids list, backup export, and help. Nothing in Settings auto-changes schedules without your confirm.
On Home, today's contracts appear as large Done buttons — one tap records the behavior and awards a gold token.
Each contract shows the child name, behavior label, and token amount. Maya's morning routine might be worth one token; evening jobs may differ.
Tap Done on Maya's morning routine. Watch the coin animation land — immediate visual feedback for the parent.
After Done, tokens update immediately in Balances. Kids see feedback in the companion once you confirm their self-reports in Approvals.
Young contracts may show an extinction-burst callout on Home — coaching copy when behavior temporarily worsens after thinning. Read it as a heads-up to stay consistent, not to escalate.
Personalization nudge cards may appear on Home — schedule thinning or saving-growth suggestions. Parents must confirm; PAL never auto-applies changes.
Open the Balances tab. Each child shows in-hand tokens versus banked savings — two jars, not a bank account.
Maya's row includes saving-growth maintenance operations in the demo — cadence coaching for bank deposits. Jacob's row stays simpler.
In-hand tokens are spendable now; banked tokens accumulate toward rewards. No sibling leaderboards or shame metrics — by design.
Tap a child row to see token history and saving cadence details. Interest accrual on banked tokens follows parent-configured rules.
Wish list items live under Balances — kids request rewards; parents approve redemptions in Approvals.
Kid web runs on your home Wi-Fi only — not the public internet. Open Settings, then Kid web.
PAL shows a LAN address and QR code when the local server is active. Phone and kid browser must share the same network.
Tap Copy link and paste into a Chromebook or tablet browser on the same Wi-Fi. Or scan the QR code from the kid device camera.
Status reads Serving on your network when active. If PAL was backgrounded, reopen it — the server pauses until the parent app is foreground again.
On iPhone, Local Network permission is required. If kid web fails to load, check Wi-Fi, foreground PAL, and that both devices are on the same subnet.
From Settings you can jump straight to Kid web whenever you need the LAN link or QR again.
Kids open the link once per browser session. The companion uses warm, kid-facing language — tokens and rewards, not banking UI.
On the kid sign-in screen, enter family password reyes — lowercase.
Tap Maya or Jacob, then enter PIN one-two-three-four. Each kid sees their own assignments and token balance.
Assignments appear as friendly jobs — I did it confirms completion. Coins wait for parent approval; delayed verification is intentional.
Kids get immediate visual feedback when they tap I did it. You stay in control — nothing counts until you confirm in Approvals.
From kid web, Maya can request a reward from her wish list. The request appears in parent Approvals — nothing auto-redeems.
Jacob's companion stays simpler in the demo — fewer saving-growth prompts. Compare whether age-appropriate defaults feel right.
Switch back to the parent app. Open Approvals — badge count shows pending kid reports.
Each pending item shows the child, contract, and timestamp. Tap Approve to award tokens or Decline to send back without credit.
Delayed verification path: kid self-report → parent Approvals. This mirrors token-economy practice — kids learn to report; parents verify.
Reward requests from kid web appear here too. Approve deducts banked tokens; decline keeps the wish pending.
After approval, Balances updates and the kid companion reflects the new total on next refresh.
Empty Approvals means everything is caught up — a good state on busy evenings.
Open Reports for charts and coaching cards. Insights tab shows frequency trends and parent-facing schedule summaries.
First-week versus now comparison cards highlight behavior change over time so you can see progress at a glance.
Switch to Trends for longer-horizon charts. Thinning and saving-growth suggestions appear as nudges — parents must confirm.
Coaching cards use plain, literature-first language. Read them as optional suggestions — nothing changes until you confirm.
Reports never auto-applies schedule changes. Every thinning or cadence adjustment requires explicit parent confirm.
Export from Settings if you need a local backup zip — no secrets are included in the archive.
Open Contracts to review seeded behavioral contracts. Each lists behavior name, token amount, and schedule type.
Tap a contract to open detail — thinning schedules, extinction-burst coaching on young contracts, and maintenance operations.
Contract detail shows token amount, target frequency, and thinning ladder. Age bands set developmental defaults only — not permanent law.
Extinction-burst callouts on young contracts explain temporary behavior spikes after schedule changes — stay consistent through the bump.
Saving-growth maintenance operations on Maya's contracts demonstrate cadence coaching — Jacob's contracts stay simpler.
Tap New contract to start from a template or from scratch. Wizard steps mirror behavioral contract best practices.
Templates include morning routine, homework block, and chore ladders — customize token amounts and schedules per child.
Archived contracts remain readable for history but stop appearing on Home Done buttons.
Settings holds Kids list, Kid web, Reviewer guide, Help, About, and local backup export.
Kids list lets you review Maya and Jacob profiles — ages drive default schedules, not fixed rules.
Help links to support email and this user guide. About shows version and design notes.
Export backup creates a local zip of contracts, tokens, and settings you control. No cloud sync required for everyday use.
Restore from backup on a new phone if you want to bring your household data with you.
Open Kid web anytime you need the LAN URL or QR for a tablet or Chromebook on the same Wi-Fi.
PAL uses token-economy language, not chore-tracker gamification. No streaks, leaderboards, or shame metrics.
Schedule thinning and saving cadence appear as age priors plus performance nudges plus parent confirm — you stay in charge of every change.
Delayed verification is intentional: kid reports, parent confirms, then tokens land. That keeps parents in the loop.
Extinction-burst coaching on Home and Contracts helps you stay consistent when behavior temporarily spikes after a schedule change.
Age bands are developmental defaults only — adjust schedules and reinforcers to fit your household.
Literature-first with room for real-family flexibility when household means require different reinforcer delivery.
PAL does not include debit or banking, a chatbot coach, cloud sync, ages under six, or a PocketBudJet expense bridge.
PAL is not kid banking — no real money, no debit cards. Tokens are symbolic reinforcers managed entirely by the parent.
